| `s3-landing` — landing; external/application landing area | `configured source paths, inbound/{lng_file_path}, inbound/archive/{lng_file_path}, and snowflake-exports` | DynamoDB process configuration supplies sftpPath and lng_file_path; basename supplies inbound filenames; Terraform OUTPUT_S3_URI fixes snowflake-exports and the export job derives gzip CSV, DDL and manifest names | `direct` |
| `s3-raw` — raw; immutable/raw processing area | prefix: `inbound/archive/{raw_file_path}{load_id}/{filename}`; normalized: `inbound/{raw_file_path}/{filename}; inbound/archive/{raw_file_path}/{load_id}/{filename}; inbound/reject/{raw_file_path}/{load_id}/{filename}` | DynamoDB raw_file_path, load_id and source basename derive raw keys; for the canonical archive template raw_file_path must supply any required trailing separator before load_id because the source code inserts none | `direct` |
| `s3-enriched` — enriched; curated transformation area | `inbound/{enr_file_path}, outbound/{enr_file_path}, inbound_archive/{enr_file_path}, outbound_archive/{enr_file_path}, outbound_reject/{enr_file_path}{load_id}` | DynamoDB enr_file_path and patternsToActions supply prefixes/actions; target_filepattern replaces wildcards with UTC timestamp and batch index; XML uses configured output naming | `direct` |
| `s3-archive` — archive; raw and enriched retention | `raw inbound/archive/{raw_file_path}{load_id}/{filename}; enriched inbound_archive/{enr_file_path}/{load_id}/{filename}; enriched outbound_archive/{enr_file_path}/{load_id}/{filename}` | raw move_files_to_archive uses canonical inbound/archive/{raw_file_path}{load_id}/{filename}; raw_file_path must supply any required separator before load_id because the code inserts none there; enriched move_s3_files combines enr_file_path, load_id and source filename with explicit separators | `direct` |
| `s3-reject` — reject; raw/enriched validation errors | `inbound/reject/{raw_file_path}{load_id}; reject_folder/{filename}; outbound_reject/{enr_file_path}{load_id}` | empty_file_check, xmlvalidation, outbound_reject paths | `direct` |
| `s3-exclusion` — exclusion; enriched inbound exclusions | `exclusion path is passed from enriched processing to email attachment Lambda` | enriched exclusion handling and Lambda S3 read/attachment code | `direct` |
| `s3-usrmt` — USRMT; business-domain exchange root | `USRMT/Inbound/Source/Medicaid_Conversion/Vistex_Claims/Medicaid_Claims` | S3 event notification prefix | `direct` |
| `s3-inbound` — inbound; partner inbound exchange | `landing inbound/{lng_file_path} and inbound/archive/{lng_file_path}; raw inbound/{raw_file_path}` | DynamoDB sftpPath, lng_file_path, raw_file_path, source_file_pattern and extractedFileName values plus source basenames derive the prefixes and filenames | `direct` |
| `s3-outbound` — outbound; partner outbound exchange | `enriched outbound/{enr_file_path}, outbound_archive/{enr_file_path}/{load_id}, and outbound_reject/{enr_file_path}{load_id}` | DynamoDB enr_file_path and patternsToActions define source/target paths; target_filepattern derives timestamped/batched output names and the transfer job uses each source basename for the remote filename | `direct` |
| `s3-snowflake-exports` — Snowflake-export; warehouse export area | `snowflake-exports` | OUTPUT_S3_URI and export README/runtime writer | `direct` |

documents.title: C.7.1 Exact Storage Limitations
documents.text:
C.7.1 Exact Storage Limitations
| Stable inventory ID | Exact limitation from inventory |
|---|---|
| `s3-code-distribution` | dev count only; physical bucket and runtime contents unverified |
| `s3-landing` | environment-resolved bucket names, partner paths and runtime object state are not asserted |
| `s3-raw` | bucket values and file-path values resolve from runtime process configuration; raw archive separation depends on configured raw_file_path ending with any needed separator before load_id; deployed/live objects were not inspected |
| `s3-enriched` | process-configuration values and runtime object state are not asserted |
| `s3-archive` | environment bucket resolution and archive contents are uninspected; the raw archive template depends on configured raw_file_path ending with any required separator before load_id |
| `s3-reject` | copy-without-delete branch is preserved as repository behavior |
| `s3-exclusion` | exact runtime prefix is configuration-driven |
| `s3-usrmt` | dev event-rule configuration only; writer identity, object movement and runtime events are not evidenced |
| `s3-inbound` | partner endpoints, resolved configuration values and runtime files are not included |
| `s3-outbound` | remote acknowledgement/retry semantics, resolved target paths and runtime delivery state are not asserted |
| `s3-snowflake-exports` | no live export assertion |

documents.title: Appendix H — Glossary and Acronym Register
documents.text:
Appendix H — Glossary and Acronym Register
Each term appears once. Acronyms are expanded in the term cell, followed by a plain-language meaning, the technical role evidenced in this guide, and the principal place a new hire will encounter it. A definition explains usage; it does not upgrade configuration or design evidence into deployed-state proof.

documents.title: H.1 Business and Integration Terms
documents.text:
H.1 Business and Integration Terms
| Term | Plain-language meaning | Technical role | Where used |
|---|---|---|---|
| H-TERM-001 — ACK (acknowledgment) | A response saying a request was processed or assigned a result | Business companion to a payment-request FGI; not transport receipt alone | `301 <-> 201`, `302 <-> 203`, `303 <-> 204` |
| H-TERM-002 — AWP (Average Wholesale Price) | A pharmaceutical reference-price measure | Derived price-list feed built from WAC data | FGI `111 / SAP_AWP` |
| H-TERM-003 — backbill | A later billing adjustment for an earlier rebate transaction | SAP transaction input transformed for Model N | FGI `210 / SAP_REBATE_BACKBILL` |
| H-TERM-004 — business grain | The real-world unit represented by one record | Basis for count and duplicate reconciliation | File, stage, transform, outbound, and target checks |
| H-TERM-005 — business key | Field set that identifies the business record | Used to match, deduplicate, enrich, and trace records | Claims, products, payments, customers, agreements |
| H-TERM-006 — canonical rollup | A teaching-level family that groups concrete variants | Connects `101` and `105` families without adding executions | Appendix B rollups and dependency map |
| H-TERM-007 — chargeback | A distributor claim for price-concession reimbursement | Inbound transactions, outbound payment requests, and acknowledgments | FGIs `207`, `213`, `301`, `201` |
| H-TERM-008 — companion file | A second input required to enrich the primary file | Supplies RODB-derived lookup results before final construction | FGIs `213`, `301`, `302` |
| H-TERM-009 — configuration alias | Alternate source name stored in configuration | Preserves config identity without creating another lineage execution | Coverage-ledger `SAP` aliases |
| H-TERM-010 — consumer acceptance | Evidence that the receiving system accepted or posted a delivery | Final proof beyond file creation or successful transfer | Model N, SAP P2R, and Axway boundaries |
| H-TERM-011 — control plane | Configuration and orchestration that direct work | Defines jobs, processes, mappings, triggers, and audit behavior | DynamoDB, EventBridge, Step Functions |
| H-TERM-012 — CPI-U (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers) | A US inflation time series | API-sourced inbound time-series feed | FGI `116 / CPIU` |
| H-TERM-013 — dependency | An upstream condition or dataset required by another flow | Can be a configured gate, business prerequisite, companion, or target | Appendix D dependency register |
| H-TERM-014 — `dependencyFlag` | Configuration switch controlling dependency enforcement | `1` enables the checked gate; `0` leaves a disabled config entry | Process configuration and audit-time-window checks |
| H-TERM-015 — direct sales | Sales reported directly rather than through an indirect claim | Transaction feed transformed for Model N loaders | FGIs `202`, `205`, `206` |
| H-TERM-016 — E4HC | One configured SAP product-master variant | First branch in the sequenced product family | FGI `105_E4HC / SAP_PRODUCT` |
| H-TERM-017 — EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) | Standardized partner-to-partner business messages | Names Axway transaction and response interfaces | FGIs `213`, `304`, `305` |
| H-TERM-018 — EDI 844 | Product transfer-account adjustment message | Axway inbound chargeback data requiring an RODB companion | FGI `213 / EDI_844` |
| H-TERM-019 — EDI 845 | Price-authorization acknowledgment/advice message | Model N outbound bid-award delivery to Axway | FGI `304 / MDN_EDI845` |
| H-TERM-020 — EDI 849 | Response to a product transfer-account adjustment | Model N outbound reconciliation delivery to Axway | FGI `305 / MDN_EDI849` |
| H-TERM-021 — exclusion | A record intentionally separated from accepted processing | Durable data outcome distinct from a failed job | Snowflake/Glue exclusion evidence and files |
| H-TERM-022 — FGI (File Group Identifier) | Business interface identifier for a configured flow | Primary key for selecting process, files, schedules, and lineage | All `1xx`, `2xx`, and `3xx` interfaces |
| H-TERM-023 — `fileGroupID` | Runtime/configuration field carrying the FGI value | Joins process, procedure, trigger, audit, and lineage records | DynamoDB items and Step Functions inputs |
| H-TERM-024 — H2R | McKesson-to-rebates integration label used in source names | Identifies McKesson customer and transaction sources | FGIs `109`, `109_MIG`, `206`, `207`, `211`, `212` |
| H-TERM-025 — inbound | Direction from an external source toward Model N | Source file enters landing/raw/model/enriched/delivery stages | SAP, McKesson, Axway, Treasury, BLS feeds |
| H-TERM-026 — LEH | Customer legal-entity hierarchy | Establishes parent/child customer relationships | FGIs `102_SEQ / SAP_LEH` and `212 / MCK_LEH` |
| H-TERM-027 — `loadId` | Identifier for one logical processing attempt/load | Correlates workflow, jobs, procedures, audit, and files | Troubleshooting and rerun decisions |
| H-TERM-028 — master data | Relatively stable customer, product, vendor, price, or UOM reference data | Must precede dependent transaction processing | `101`–`116` families |
| H-TERM-029 — McKesson | External distributor/source organization | Supplies customer and transaction files in the H2R chain | FGIs `109`, `109_MIG`, `206`, `207`, `211`, `212` |
| H-TERM-030 — Medicaid | Government rebate/payment business domain | Has request, acknowledgment, and dedicated workflow components | FGIs `303`, `204`; Medicaid state machine/jobs |
| H-TERM-031 — migration | Controlled initial/history loading rather than regular incremental flow | Uses distinct FGI variants and sometimes output paths | `101_MIG`, `101_MIG_STATUS_SPLIT`, `109_MIG` |
| H-TERM-032 — Model N | Receiving/source commercial platform in the integration | Receives inbound masters/transactions and produces outbound requests/EDI | Core business-system boundary |
| H-TERM-033 — NDC (National Drug Code) | Pharmaceutical product identifier | Used in product validation, exclusions, and contract

documents.title: H.2 AWS and Runtime Terms
documents.text:
H.2 AWS and Runtime Terms
| Term | Plain-language meaning | Technical role | Where used |
|---|---|---|---|
| H-TERM-048 — ARN (Amazon Resource Name) | AWS resource identifier | Connects policies, functions, state machines, and targets | Terraform and Step Functions definitions |
| H-TERM-049 — ASL (Amazon States Language) | JSON language for Step Functions workflows | Defines states, transitions, inputs, retry, and catch behavior | Environment state files |
| H-TERM-050 — AWS (Amazon Web Services) | Cloud platform hosting the integration runtime | Provides compute, orchestration, storage, security, and logs | Appendix A component register |
| H-TERM-051 — CloudWatch Events | Earlier AWS name/API surface for event rules | Terraform-configured schedule and event targets | Trigger source files and EventBridge inventory |
| H-TERM-052 — CloudWatch Logs | Central AWS log storage | Holds Lambda, Glue, Step Functions, VPC, and Transfer evidence | Incident collection and verification |
| H-TERM-053 — cron expression | Compact schedule syntax | Configures recurring EventBridge invocations in UTC | Appendix D 134 scheduled rules |
| H-TERM-054 — DLQ (dead-letter queue) | Queue for messages/events that could not be delivered | Failure-isolation capability; caller configuration varies | Lambda module and EventBridge target capability |
| H-TERM-055 — DynamoDB | AWS key-value/document database | Stores process, job, procedure, audit, and SFTP mapping contracts | Fourteen configured tables |
| H-TERM-056 — EventBridge | AWS event-routing and scheduling service | Starts Lambda, Step Functions, or Glue targets | Trigger/cadence register |
| H-TERM-057 — event pattern | Rule matching an event rather than a clock | Selects S3 object events for a target | Disabled Medicaid S3 rule with missing schedule |
| H-TERM-058 — Glue | AWS managed data-integration runtime | Runs Spark and Python Shell jobs for transform/export/transfer | Fourteen configured jobs |
| H-TERM-059 — IAM (Identity and Access Management) | AWS permissions and role system | Controls service execution, triggers, logs, and transfer access | Runtime and platform Terraform |
| H-TERM-060 — KMS (Key Management Service) | AWS encryption-key service | Supports configured data-at-rest encryption branches | S3/security controls |
| H-TERM-061 — Lambda | AWS event-driven function compute | Initializes, audits, retrieves, notifies, scrapes, updates, and provisions | Nine inventoried functions |
| H-TERM-062 — S3 (Simple Storage Service) | AWS object storage | Holds artifacts and every logical file-processing zone | Code, landing, raw, enriched, archive, exchange |
| H-TERM-063 — Secrets Manager | AWS secret-storage service | Supplies database, application, Entra, and SFTP credential families | Lambda/Glue/provisioner references |
| H-TERM-064 — security group | Virtual firewall attached to AWS resources | Restricts network paths for Lambda, Glue, and Transfer | VPC configuration |
| H-TERM-065 — SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) | Encrypted file-transfer protocol | Partner-facing movement into or out of S3-backed paths | Transfer Family and Glue transfer job |
| H-TERM-066 — SQS (Simple Queue Service) | AWS message queue | Underlies configured Lambda dead-letter capability | Observability/failure controls |
| H-TERM-067 — Step Functions | AWS workflow orchestration service | Coordinates Lambda/Glue tasks, branches, waits, retries, and maps | Six workflow families, 18 variants |
| H-TERM-068 — state machine | Executable Step Functions workflow definition | Owns `StartAt`, states, transitions, and terminal behavior | Inbound, outbound, queue, Medicaid, tests |
| H-TERM-069 — Task state | Workflow state that invokes work | Calls Lambda or synchronous Glue integration | ASL task boundaries |
| H-TERM-070 — Choice state | Conditional workflow branch | Routes by fields such as status or wait decision | Queue and core workflows |
| H-TERM-071 — Wait state | Workflow pause | Delays before returning to a check | Queue-control loop |
| H-TERM-072 — Map state | Iterates over a list of items | Runs a per-item Glue task with configured concurrency | Queue-trigger workflow |
| H-TERM-073 — Parallel state | Runs branches concurrently | Represents concurrent workflow segments where configured | ASL orchestration patterns |
| H-TERM-074 — Retry | Automatic repeat policy for a failed task | Controls attempts, interval, and backoff for named errors | ASL task definitions |
| H-TERM-075 — Catch | Failure-routing rule | Sends an error to a recovery/notification branch | ASL task definitions |
| H-TERM-076 — task token | Callback correlation token | Lets asynchronous work report completion to the waiting workflow | Step Functions/Glue argument contracts |
| H-TERM-077 — Transfer Family | AWS managed transfer service | Hosts the VPC-attached service-managed SFTP endpoint | Platform boundary |
| H-TERM-078 — VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) | Isolated AWS network | Contains private subnets, routes, security groups, and service paths | Lambda/Glue/Transfer/database connectivity |
| H-TERM-079 — subnet | Address range and placement boundary inside a VPC | Places workloads in private network segments | Lambda and Transfer configuration |
| H-TERM-080 — X-Ray | AWS distributed-tracing service | Module-supported Lambda tracing; inherited setting is disabled | Observability register |
| H-TERM-081 — scheduler target | Resource invoked when a configured rule fires | Associates rule, role, input, and Lambda/Step Functions/Glue target | EventBridge inventory |
| H-TERM-082 — `safe_input` | Sanitized business input recorded for a trigger | Shows FGI/source/status fields without sensitive payload data | Appendix D trigger rows |

documents.title: H.3 Snowflake, RODB, and Data Terms
documents.text:
H.3 Snowflake, RODB, and Data Terms
| Term | Plain-language meaning | Technical role | Where used |
|---|---|---|---|
| H-TERM-083 — Snowflake | Cloud data platform used for staged transformations | Hosts configured procedure/object lineage and export boundaries | Model job and Appendix E |
| H-TERM-084 — SQL (Structured Query Language) | Language for querying and changing relational data | Defines procedures, joins, transforms, DQC, and exports | Snowflake and RODB evidence |
| H-TERM-085 — DDL (Data Definition Language) | SQL that creates or changes database objects | Defines procedures, tables, streams, and schemas | Missing Snowflake source/deployment boundary |
| H-TERM-086 — DML (Data Manipulation Language) | SQL that reads or changes rows | Implements select, insert, update, delete, and merge behavior | Procedure and diagnostic reasoning |
| H-TERM-087 — stored procedure | Named database program | Executes ordered stage, transform, enrich, audit, or export work | 70 configured rows / 47 canonical names |
| H-TERM-088 — VARIANT | Snowflake semi-structured data type/layer | Holds parsed XML-like source before structured extraction | Selected XML-style 3xx flows |
| H-TERM-089 — STG (stage) | Structured intermediate landing layer | Holds source-shaped rows before business transformation | `STAGE.STG_*` objects |
| H-TERM-090 — TRANS (transformation) | Working/current-load transformation layer | Combines, enriches, and reshapes rows before output | `COMMON.TRANS_*` and related objects |
| H-TERM-091 — current load | Rows selected for the processing attempt in scope | Prevents old and new data from being mixed in export/recovery reasoning | TRANS and export boundaries |
| H-TERM-092 — OTBD (output-bound) | Downstream-ready table boundary | Supplies rows for output construction or merge target | `ENRICH.OTBD_*` objects |
| H-TERM-093 — stream | Snowflake change-capture object | Supports insert/update audit counts in supplied designs | `COMMON.stream_*`, `stream_sap_p2r_ds` |
| H-TERM-094 — DQC (data-quality check) | Rule testing whether data meets required conditions | Separates accepted, failed, or excluded records | Snowflake design and exclusion evidence |
| H-TERM-095 — RODB | the Model N Oracle-backed lookup boundary called RODB in reviewed code/configuration; expansion not established | Supplies contract, claim, product, payment, and organization enrichment | Configured flows `213`, `301`, `302` |
| H-TERM-096 — Oracle | Database technology/client used by the RODB path | Glue/Lambda uses private connectivity and credentials for lookups | RODB job and security boundary |
| H-TERM-097 — lookup key | Field used to find enrichment rows | Correlates stage data with RODB records | Claim/product, payment ID, external contract ID |
| H-TERM-098 — query configuration | Committed query text/object references in environment JSON | Proves configured lookup intent, not execution or database DDL | RODB source-metadata records |
| H-TERM-099 — `source_sql_verified` | Evidence flag for implementation-source review | False for every Appendix E procedure/object because R04 is missing | Snowflake/RODB inventory |
| H-TERM-100 — MNRC | Schema/prefix used by named RODB objects | Qualifies contract, claim, sales, payment, program, and organization sources | `MNRC.*` lookup objects |
| H-TERM-101 — MERGE | SQL operation combining matched and unmatched rows | Documented way to write selected OTBD targets | Supplied business designs |
| H-TERM-102 — Time Travel | Snowflake historical-data capability | Evidence-dependent option for inspecting or restoring earlier table state | Rollback-target objects |
| H-TERM-103 — query history | Database record of executed statements | Runtime proof for procedure/DDL/DML investigation | Snowflake evidence collection |
| H-TERM-104 — cardinality | Number of rows produced for each input/business key | Detects legitimate one-to-many results versus duplication | RODB joins and reconciliation |
| H-TERM-105 — aggregation | Combining multiple rows into grouped values | Builds package or business-level output structures | Rebate and contract-domain designs |
| H-TERM-106 — join | Relating rows through matching fields | Connects stage records to contract/payment/product/organization data | RODB and Snowflake transformations |
| H-TERM-107 — idempotency | Ability to repeat work without duplicate business effects | Required proof before same-load or new-load recovery | Procedures, audit, files, target posting |
| H-TERM-108 — reconciliation | Comparing evidence across stages at matching identities/grains | Establishes what happened before correction or replay | Incident and rerun workflow |
| H-TERM-109 — rollback | Restoring future behavior or data to an earlier approved state | Separate from replaying or undoing already-delivered business effects | Part V change safety |
| H-TERM-110 — rerun / replay | Re-executing part or all of a business flow | Allowed only after prior durable effects and duplicate risk are proven | Part V recovery gate |

documents.title: H.4 Engineering, Identity, and Evidence Terms
documents.text:
H.4 Engineering, Identity, and Evidence Terms
| Term | Plain-language meaning | Technical role | Where used |
|---|---|---|---|
| H-TERM-111 — artifact | Packaged deployable code | Connects source/workflow output to Terraform-selected Lambda/Glue code | R02/R03/R10 -> IaC chain |
| H-TERM-112 — audit trail | Time-ordered records showing processing status/counts | Correlates workflows, jobs, procedures, files, and target outcomes | DynamoDB, Snowflake, logs |
| H-TERM-113 — checkpoint | Known durable boundary reached by a run | Narrows recovery to the earliest unproven or failed boundary | Workflow/job/data recovery |
| H-TERM-114 — CI/CD (continuous integration / continuous delivery) | Automated validation, packaging, and deployment workflow | Builds artifacts and applies IaC/configuration through shared tooling | R17–R21 and repository workflows |
| H-TERM-115 — configured / deployed / executed | Three different evidence states | Separates source intent, active runtime state, and observed run history | Every inventory and investigation |
| H-TERM-116 — correlation identity | Set of IDs needed to join evidence | Usually includes FGI, source, load, process, job, execution, and object/file identity | Troubleshooting worksheet |
| H-TERM-117 — deployment proof | Evidence that a specific revision/config is active | Requires individual deploy-step plus deployed version/digest, or applicable IaC/live-table proof | Part V ownership/change chapters |
| H-TERM-118 — dev / QA / prod / sandbox | Environment labels for development, testing, production-named, and isolated work | Scope configuration variants without assuming promotion or active state | Schedules, workflows, config repositories |
| H-TERM-119 — evidence class | Label describing how a fact was established | Distinguishes code, configuration, design, synthesis, inference, and gaps | Inventories and appendices |
| H-TERM-120 — IaC (infrastructure as code) | Versioned source describing cloud resources | Terraform modules define AWS runtime/platform components | R01, R09, R23 |
| H-TERM-121 — immutable artifact | Versioned package that is not edited in place | Safe deployment/rollback unit for Lambda and Glue | Artifact promotion chain |
| H-TERM-122 — `jobId` | Identifier for a configured job step | Orders and selects Glue/Lambda work within a process | Job configuration and workflow input |
| H-TERM-123 — `jobRunId` | Identifier for one job execution | Joins run details, process logs, and CDW audit records | DynamoDB audit tables |
| H-TERM-124 — `missing_locally` | Approved source is absent from the reviewed workspace | Prevents source verification without implying the component does not exist | R04 Snowflake repository |
| H-TERM-125 — `processId` | Identifier for the configured FGI/source process | Links process, job, procedure, and audit configuration | DynamoDB and Appendix E mappings |
| H-TERM-126 — process log | Durable run-status record at process/job grain | Supports dependency checks and investigation | `bay-modeln-process-log-table` |
| H-TERM-127 — reusable workflow | Shared CI/CD workflow called by several repositories | Centralizes Lambda, Glue, or DynamoDB build/apply mechanics | R19 and R20 |
| H-TERM-128 — source of truth | Most authoritative available evidence for a claim | Prefers owning code/config/live proof over summaries or intuition | Evidence-first workflow |
| H-TERM-129 — Terraform | IaC tool used to define/apply AWS resources | Connects modules, variables, artifacts, schedules, and permissions | Runtime/platform repositories |
| H-TERM-130 — UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) | Common time standard independent of local timezone | Required interpretation for all listed cron schedules and evidence timestamps | Appendix D and incident timelines |

documents.title: H.5 Evidence-Limit Reminder
documents.text:
H.5 Evidence-Limit Reminder
The glossary is descriptive, not authoritative implementation source. When a term points to configured or supplied-design behavior, resolve the current environment, exact identity, active revision, and runtime evidence before acting. In particular, no glossary definition supplies the missing Snowflake SQL or converts the incident XML from metadata-only evidence into approved payload access.

documents.title: Appendix I — Weekend Master Assessment
documents.text:
Appendix I — Weekend Master Assessment
Complete this assessment after the weekend study sequence without using the answer key. It tests integration reasoning rather than memorized inventory counts. Each question is worth 2 points, one point per independently scorable answer atom, for 56 points total. Production authority is never granted by a score.

documents.title: I.1 Questions
documents.text:
I.1 Questions
| ID | Domain | Question | Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| I-Q01 | Mental model | A Terraform rule exists in source. Name the three evidence states you must keep separate before saying it ran. | 2 |
| I-Q02 | Mental model | Build a minimum correlation key for tracing one business attempt across configuration, workflow, job, and file evidence. | 2 |
| I-Q03 | Mental model | Explain why a green Step Functions execution can coexist with an incomplete business outcome. | 2 |
| I-Q04 | Mental model | Contrast a canonical FGI rollup with a concrete configured FGI/source pair. | 2 |
| I-Q05 | FGI/dependencies | Reconstruct the supported `105 -> 103 -> 114` chain and identify which records are derived. | 2 |
| I-Q06 | FGI/dependencies | Reconstruct the McKesson shared-stage chain beginning at `211` and ending at hierarchy output. | 2 |
| I-Q07 | FGI/dependencies | What relationship connects FGI `301` and FGI `201`, and what proof is still required after both run? | 2 |
| I-Q08 | FGI/dependencies | For FGI `202`, distinguish the customer-master entry from the product-master gate. | 2 |
| I-Q09 | Files/directions | Trace FGI `101_SEQ` from source pattern/path to its two configured Model N output variants. | 2 |
| I-Q10 | Files/directions | Trace FGI `301` across Model N source, RODB companion, and SAP target file boundaries. | 2 |
| I-Q11 | Files/directions | Name the primary and companion inputs for FGI `213` and the final Model N delivery family. | 2 |
| I-Q12 | Files/directions | Differentiate archive, reject, and exclusion outcomes during an investigation. | 2 |
| I-Q13 | Runtime | Starting from a business EventBridge rule, name the evidence chain through target, workflow, task, and logs. | 2 |
| I-Q14 | Runtime | Distinguish an ASL Retry/Catch action from an operator-approved business rerun. | 2 |
| I-Q15 | Runtime | Describe the queue-control loop using its state types and its terminal work-dispatch behavior. | 2 |
| I-Q16 | Runtime | Interpret a disabled cron rule and the disabled Medicaid event-pattern rule whose schedule is missing. | 2 |
| I-Q17 | Snowflake/RODB | Give the supported XML-style data-layer sequence and state why it cannot be imposed on every FGI. | 2 |
| I-Q18 | Snowflake/RODB | State the FGI `301` OTBD naming conflict and the safe resolution method. | 2 |
| I-Q19 | Snowflake/RODB | Classify FGIs `213`, `301`, `302`, and `303` by RODB usage. | 2 |
| I-Q20 | Snowflake/RODB | Explain “RODB query configuration verified” while `source_sql_verified=false`. | 2 |
| I-Q21 | Troubleshooting | Before opening logs for a failed run, which identities and effective configuration must be fixed in scope? | 2 |
| I-Q22 | Troubleshooting | For incident `0009343`, what may this guide state, and what evidence remains intentionally unavailable? | 2 |
| I-Q23 | Troubleshooting | Before correcting a suspected Snowflake transformation, name the two proof categories required. | 2 |
| I-Q24 | Troubleshooting | What separates a same-load recovery from starting a new `loadId` safely? | 2 |
| I-Q25 | Repositories/deployment | Trace direct Lambda code promotion with the R-rows and distinguish it from R01 infrastructure/baseline deployment. | 2 |
| I-Q26 | Repositories/deployment | A QA process-config value is wrong. Name the source owner and promotion/tooling owners, then the live proof. | 2 |
| I-Q27 | Repositories/deployment | A Snowflake procedure body is wrong while R04 remains unavailable. What is the allowed ownership path? | 2 |
| I-Q28 | Repositories/deployment | Why does rolling back code/configuration not automatically complete business recovery? | 2 |

documents.title: I.2 Exact Answer Key and Atomic Rubric
documents.text:
I.2 Exact Answer Key and Atomic Rubric
Award each atom only when the response states the required distinction or relationship. Equivalent plain language is acceptable; an answer that merely lists a term without the stated relationship earns no atom.

| ID | Exact answer | Atom A — 1 point | Atom B — 1 point |
|---|---|---|---|
| I-Q01 | Keep configured source, deployed/active state, and observed execution separate. | Names configured versus deployed. | Separately requires execution evidence. |
| I-Q02 | Use FGI + source system + `loadId`, then process/job/execution/file identity as available. | Includes FGI, source, and load. | Includes at least one job/execution identity and file/object identity. |
| I-Q03 | Workflow success proves orchestration completion, not file delivery, target posting, or acknowledgment. | States technical success is limited to the workflow boundary. | Requires downstream receipt/posting/ack proof. |
| I-Q04 | A rollup groups a design family; a concrete pair has configured source identity, files, jobs/procedures, and possibly schedules. | Rollup is design-only and not another execution. | Concrete pair is configuration/lineage identity. |
| I-Q05 | Product family `105` precedes UOM `103`; alternate UOM `114` is derived from `103`. | Gives `105 -> 103`. | Gives `103 -> 114` and identifies `114` as derived. |
| I-Q06 | `211` creates the shared stage; `206` and `207` split direct/chargeback; `212` derives hierarchy from their stages. | Gives `211 -> 206/207`. | Gives `206/207 -> 212` with hierarchy role. |
| I-Q07 | `301` is the chargeback payment request and `201` its acknowledgment; correlation plus SAP acceptance/posting is still required. | Correctly identifies request/ack direction. | Requires correlated target business proof. |
| I-Q08 | `101_SEQ -> 202` is a disabled `dependencyFlag=0` entry; `105_USRI -> 202` is enabled with `dependencyFlag=1`. | Customer entry is disabled/not enforced. | Product gate is enabled/enforced. |
| I-Q09 | Source is `Inbound/Source/SAP/CustomerMaster/` with `SAP_P2R_Customers_Master_*.xml`; outputs are E4HC and USRI community variants under `/Inbound/PharmaCommunity/`. | Correct source path and pattern. | Both configured E4HC/USRI target variants and target path. |
| I-Q10 | Model N source is NightlyDistRebatesClaim XML; companion is `Chargeback_Payment_Request_<datetime>.csv`; target is SAP chargeback-payment-request XML path. | Correct Model N source and RODB companion. | Correct SAP target family/path. |
| I-Q11 | Primary is `*_844_*.csv` under Axway EDI_844; companion is `EDI_RODB_<datetime>.csv`; output is chargeback-loader CSV to Model N. | Correct primary plus companion. | Correct Model N output family/direction. |
| I-Q12 | Archive retains processed objects; reject holds validation errors; exclusion holds intentionally filtered business records. | Correct archive versus reject distinction. | Correct exclusion as data outcome, not job failure. |
| I-Q13 | Inspect configured rule/status/input and target; then Step Functions execution/state task, named Lambda/Glue run, and complete CloudWatch logs. | Rule/status/input and target/workflow evidence. | Task/run plus complete log evidence. |
| I-Q14 | Retry/Catch is definition-controlled task handling inside an execution; a business rerun is an operator decision after durable-effect reconciliation. | Correct ASL-local behavior. | Requires reconciliation/approval before rerun. |
| I-Q15 | Task checks the queue, Choice selects wait or work, Wait loops, and Map dispatches per-item Glue work. | Names Task/Choice/Wait loop. | Names Map terminal dispatch behavior. |
| I-Q16 | Disabled cron means configured but not scheduled to fire; missing schedule identifies an event-pattern rule, also disabled. | Does not infer execution from disabled cron. | Correctly distinguishes event pattern from absent cron. |
| I-Q17 | Supported selected XML path is VARIANT -> STG -> TRANS/current-load -> DQC -> OTBD; CSV/other FGIs may omit layers. | Correct layer sequence. | States it is evidence-specific, not universal. |
| I-Q18 | Supplied design names `ENRICHV1.OTBD_MN_PMNT_CHBK_REQ`; synthesis names `ENRICH.OTBD_MN_PMNT_CHBK_REQ`; resolve via approved SQL/live metadata. | Names both conflicting targets. | Requires owner SQL or approved live metadata before querying/changing. |
| I-Q19 | `213`, `301`, and `302` have configured RODB flows; `303` is the committed non-RODB comparison. | Correctly groups the three RODB FGIs. | Correctly identifies `303` as non-RODB. |
| I-Q20 | Committed query text/object references are evidenced, but missing Snowflake source/database inspection prevents SQL/DDL/execution/row verification. | Explains what query configuration proves. | Explains what `source_sql_verified=false` withholds. |
| I-Q21 | Fix FGI/source/load/process/job/execution identity, then read effective job/process/source/procedure configuration for that environment. | Establishes correlation identities. | Establishes effective environment configuration before logs. |
| I-Q22 | The guide may use the sanitized metadata and structural case study; XML payload/content and sensitive production values remain excluded. | Identifies metadata-only allowed evidence. | Explicitly excludes payload/content/values. |
| I-Q23 | Obtain owning procedure SQL/query history and layer-by-layer row evidence; also reconcile audit/file/target side effects at the same grain. | Requires SQL/query and data-layer proof. | Requires cross-system side-effect reconciliation. |
| I-Q24 | Same-load recovery requires idempotency/checkpoint proof; a new load requires authoritative source plus full prior-effect and duplicate-risk reconciliation. | States same-load idempotency/checkpoint gate. | States new-load source/prior-effects/duplicate gate. |
| I-Q25 | R02 calls R19; R19 publishes a versioned artifact and invokes R17 `deployer.py` directly on the existing Lambda. R01 separately provisions/configures and may select a baseline. | Correct R02/R19/R17 direct code-promotion chain. |

documents.title: I.3 Score Interpretation
documents.text:
I.3 Score Interpretation
| Score | Interpretation | Required next action | Production implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50–56 | Ready for a supervised trace and explanation | Review any missed atoms, then perform the capstone with a mentor | No independent production authority |
| 42–49 | Core model is present but uneven | Restudy the domains containing misses; repeat those questions and traces | Remain supervised |
| 34–41 | Material reasoning gaps | Repeat required Parts II–V selections and use Appendices B–G for guided lookup | Do not lead a runtime investigation |
| 0–33 | Foundations not yet reliable | Restart the weekend path from Part I and schedule mentor review | No operational action |

**Safety override:** A high score does not compensate for inventing SQL, exposing incident payloads, treating configured state as execution, or replaying before durable-effect reconciliation. Any such answer must be corrected before the capstone is accepted.

documents.title: Appendix J — New-Hire Capstone and Quick Reference
documents.text:
Appendix J — New-Hire Capstone and Quick Reference
The capstone is a supervised explanation and trace exercise. It tests whether the new hire can connect business identity, file movement, orchestration, data transformation, evidence, and repository ownership without turning configuration into an unsupported runtime claim.

documents.title: J.1 Fifteen-to-Twenty-Minute End-to-End Talk Track
documents.text:
J.1 Fifteen-to-Twenty-Minute End-to-End Talk Track
Aim for 17–18 minutes. Use names from the guide, but explain relationships rather than reciting inventories.

| Time | Topic | Required content | Evidence boundary to state aloud |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–2:00 | Purpose and actors | Model N exchanges master, transaction, payment, and EDI data with SAP, McKesson, Axway, and public APIs | Business intent is not current runtime proof |
| 2:00–4:30 | Identity and configuration | FGI + source selects process/jobs/procedures/files; `loadId` and run IDs correlate one attempt | Alias/rollup differs from a concrete pair |
| 4:30–7:00 | Inbound lane | Source/SFTP/API -> landing -> raw -> model/Snowflake -> enriched -> Model N delivery | Each boundary needs file/run/audit evidence |
| 7:00–9:30 | Outbound lane | Model N export -> model/RODB/Snowflake -> enriched -> SAP/Axway; payment requests later pair to acknowledgments | Delivery is not posting or acknowledgment |
| 9:30–12:00 | Runtime control | EventBridge target -> Step Functions -> Lambda/Glue tasks, branches, retries/catches, logs | Configured/disabled schedules do not prove execution |
| 12:00–14:30 | Data path | Selected flows use VARIANT/STG/TRANS/DQC/OTBD; `213`, `301`, `302` add RODB companions | Layers are evidence-specific; SQL source is missing |
| 14:30–16:30 | Evidence and recovery | Correlate config, execution, logs, files, rows, audit, target, ack; choose rerun only after durable-effect proof | Technical success and business completion differ |
| 16:30–18:00 | Ownership and change | Branch A: R01 resource/baseline IaC. Branch B: R02/R03/R10 -> R19 -> artifact -> R17 direct deploy | Overall workflow success can conceal a continued deploy-step failure; verify logs and deployed digest |

documents.title: J.2 Whiteboard-from-Memory Sequence
documents.text:
J.2 Whiteboard-from-Memory Sequence
Draw boxes and arrows in this order, then annotate every arrow with the identity or evidence that crosses it:

1. Put the concrete `fileGroupID / sourceSystemName` pair at the top-left; write the environment beside it.
2. Add the source actor and exact configured filename/path contract.
3. Add SFTP, API, Model N export, or source-S3 boundary as evidenced for that pair.
4. Add the EventBridge or other start mechanism; label configured status and UTC schedule when present.
5. Add the target Step Functions workflow and its execution identity.
6. Add audit, initialization, fetch, error, and domain-specific Lambda tasks actually used by the flow.
7. Add ordered Glue jobs and their `jobRunId` evidence.
8. Add Snowflake VARIANT/STG/TRANS/DQC/exclusion/OTBD boxes only where evidence supports them.
9. Add the RODB companion branch for `213`, `301`, or `302`; leave it absent for the committed `303` comparison.
10. Add enriched/outbound S3 objects, archive/reject/exclusion outcomes, and transfer task.
11. Add Model N, SAP P2R, or Axway receipt; for payment requests, add the later acknowledgment FGI.
12. Under the drawing, list the owning R-rows and write “configured,” “deployed,” “executed,” or “unverified” beside each claim.

documents.title: J.3 Three Trace Scenarios
documents.text:
J.3 Three Trace Scenarios
| Scenario | Start and route | Required finish | Stop conditions |
|---|---|---|---|
| J-TRACE-01 — `101_SEQ / SAP_CUSTOMER` | Customer-master XML -> inbound workflow -> `JB01–JB05`; `PROC_XML_TO_VARIANT_SEQ` then customer variant extract | Reconcile both E4HC/USRI community output variants under `/Inbound/PharmaCommunity/` and Model N acceptance | Stop if environment schedule/state, exact load, output set, or acceptance is unproven |
| J-TRACE-02 — `213 / EDI_844` | Axway `*_844_*.csv` + `EDI_RODB_<datetime>.csv`; CSV stage -> Axway enrich -> documented STG/TRANS boundary | Reconcile chargeback-loader CSV, Model N receipt, row cardinality, exclusions, and audits | Stop if companion correlation, query result, physical inferred names, or target receipt is unresolved |
| J-TRACE-03 — `301 / MDN_CHARGEBACK` | Nightly claim XML + chargeback RODB companion; three configured procedures; VARIANT/STG/TRANS/OTBD | Reconcile SAP payment-request file, posting evidence, and later FGI `201` acknowledgment | Stop on `ENRICH`/`ENRICHV1` ambiguity, missing SQL, prior side effects, or metadata-only incident limits |

documents.title: Scenario Delivery Pattern
documents.text:
Scenario Delivery Pattern
For each trace, speak in the same six moves: identify the pair and environment; read effective configuration; establish execution/run identities; follow files and rows at matching grain; verify target/ack outcome; then name the owning source and the earliest safe recovery boundary. If evidence is absent, say “not inspected” or “not established,” not “failed” or “does not exist.”

documents.title: J.4 New-Hire Readiness Rubric
documents.text:
J.4 New-Hire Readiness Rubric
| Capability | Ready behavior | Needs-coaching signal | Mentor verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mental model | Separates business, control, data, and evidence boundaries | Describes one undifferentiated pipeline | Ask for configured/deployed/executed distinctions |
| FGI lookup | Resolves concrete pair, aliases, files, dependencies, and cadence | Starts from FGI alone or treats rollup as execution | Give an unfamiliar Appendix B pair |
| Runtime trace | Correlates rule, workflow state, Lambda/Glue run, and logs | Stops at a green state-machine result | Require target and business evidence |
| Data trace | Uses supported layers and business grain; handles cardinality | Invents missing tables/SQL or compares unlike counts | Trace one RODB and one non-RODB flow |
| Evidence hygiene | Labels configured, documented, inferred, missing, and uninspected | Converts design/source presence into live-state claims | Challenge one source limitation |
| Recovery judgment | Reconciles durable effects before retry/replay | Restarts from source or clears audit to remove symptoms | Review same-load versus new-load choice |
| Ownership | Selects owning R-row plus workflow/tooling/deployment chain | Edits adjacent repo or live runtime first | Ask one Lambda, config, and Snowflake change |
| Communication | Gives concise facts, hypotheses, gaps, next proof, and stop condition | Blends observations and assumptions | Deliver one scenario in five minutes |

**Capstone acceptance:** The mentor should observe all eight ready behaviors across the talk track and at least two trace scenarios, including J-TRACE-03. A missed safety distinction requires correction and replay of that section, regardless of the Appendix I score.

documents.title: J.5 Monday Handoff Checklist
documents.text:
J.5 Monday Handoff Checklist
- Confirm the assigned mentor, target environment, read-only access boundaries, and escalation route.
- Review the `missing_locally` Snowflake source limitation and the incident XML metadata-only rule.
- Select one low-risk historical run with approved evidence; record FGI, source, `loadId`, process, execution, job, and file identities.
- Read the exact environment's process, job, source-metadata, and stored-procedure configuration before opening logs.
- Trace the selected run through workflow states, Lambda/Glue logs, S3/SFTP objects, Snowflake/RODB boundaries, audit, and target evidence.
- State every finding as configured, documented, deployed, executed, inferred, not inspected, or unresolved.
- Review one dependency gate and one disabled schedule with the mentor; explain why neither is inferred from naming.
- Walk one code change through R02/R03/R10, R19 publication, and R17 direct deploy; inspect the continued deploy-step logs and deployed version/digest. Contrast it with an R01 infrastructure/baseline apply.
- Practice the same-load/new-load recovery decision without executing a replay.
- Capture open evidence gaps and owners; do not “close” a gap with a synthesized claim.

documents.title: J.6 One-Page Quick-Reference Study Card
documents.text: J.6 One-Page Quick-Reference Study Card

documents.title: Start Every Trace
documents.text:
Start Every Trace
| Ask | Record | First lookup | Do not infer |
|---|---|---|---|
| What business flow? | FGI + source + direction + environment | Appendices B/C | Alias or rollup as extra execution |
| Which attempt? | `loadId`, process, execution, `jobId`, `jobRunId` | Effective config and audit | Same name means same run |
| How did it start? | Rule/event, status, UTC schedule, target/input | Appendix D + Terraform | Configured or enabled means it fired |
| Where is the data? | Source, landing/raw, stage/transform, output, target | C/E plus scoped runtime evidence | Missing evidence means missing data |

documents.title: Evidence Order
documents.text:
Evidence Order
| Order | Boundary | Minimum proof | Stop when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Effective configuration | Exact environment key/value and source revision | FGI/source/process cannot be resolved |
| 2 | Workflow | Execution input/output, state path, timestamps | Execution identity or branch is ambiguous |
| 3 | Lambda/Glue | Function/job revision, run/attempt, complete logs | Logs are partial or belong to another run |
| 4 | File movement | Exact object/path, size/count/time, archive/reject/exclusion | Source and destination cannot be correlated |
| 5 | Snowflake/RODB | Layer rows/query history at matching grain | SQL/name/current-load predicate is unresolved |
| 6 | Consumer | Receipt/import/posting plus acknowledgment when applicable | Only transfer or technical-success evidence exists |

documents.title: Recovery and Ownership
documents.text:
Recovery and Ownership
| Situation | Safe response | Owner lookup | Never do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task failed, effects unknown | Reconcile every durable boundary first | Part V + Appendix E | Blind retry or audit deletion |
| Code behavior wrong | Use R19/R17 direct deploy; verify individual step and deployed version/digest | Part V Chapters 38–40 + Appendix F | Trust overall workflow success or patch live code |
| Infrastructure/baseline wrong | Change R01 Terraform through reviewed plan/apply; verify resource config | Part V Chapter 38 + Appendix F | Treat IaC apply as proof of later code promotion |
| Config value wrong | Change target environment JSON through approved workflow; verify exact live key | R05–R07 or R11–R14 + R20/R18 | Edit another environment or assume promotion |
| Procedure SQL wrong | Obtain R04 owner/source or controlled manual DDL process | R04 + Appendix E | Substitute Glue/config change for SQL ownership |
| Request delivered, outcome unknown | Verify target posting and correlated acknowledgment | Appendices B–D | Call file transfer “business complete” |

documents.title: How to Keep This Guide Current
documents.text:
How to Keep This Guide Current
Use this checklist when approved evidence changes. Update the manuscript and its source inventories in their owning task; never hand-edit an appendix fact without reconciling its upstream record.

1. Identify the changed evidence class: code, Terraform, environment configuration, business design, runtime observation, incident metadata, or repository ownership.
2. Reconcile the concrete identity first: environment, FGI/source pair, component/resource, repository R-row, procedure/object, schedule rule, or source-register ID.
3. Update canonical inventory facts before prose: preserve stable IDs where the entity is unchanged; add a new ID only for a genuinely new entity.
4. Recompute exact counts and compare environment variants. Keep disabled, missing, inferred, unresolved, `missing_locally`, and `source_sql_verified=false` states explicit.
5. Update every affected lookup: component, FGI, file, trigger/dependency, procedure/object, repository, glossary, assessment answer, capstone trace, and source register.
6. Keep business/design evidence separate from deployment and execution evidence. Add timestamps and evidence grain to time-bounded observations.
7. Do not copy secret values, account identifiers, incident XML payloads, unrelated production data, or unsafe absolute paths into the guide.
8. Re-run table-budget, stable-ID, question/answer/points, glossary uniqueness, heading, code-fence, coverage, drafting, and sensitive-data checks.
9. Have an owning engineer review changed runtime/SQL/configuration claims and a new-hire reader test the affected explanation.
10. Record unresolved gaps and next owner/proof. Never fill a missing box merely to make the guide look complete.
